title: Sell Mineral Rights in McKenzie, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in McKenzie, AL | Offer
metaDescription: McKenzie, Conecuh County mineral owner in the south Alabama Smackover trend? Get an honest cash offer built from your real lease history.
heroLead: McKenzie sits on the Conecuh-Butler County line, a small railroad town whose mineral history is tied more to the region's broader Smackover leasing cycles than to any single major discovery close by.
intro: If you have inherited a McKenzie-area mineral interest, chances are it connects to farmland or timber acreage that was leased at some point during one of south Alabama's periodic waves of oil and gas exploration interest, whether or not a well was ever actually drilled on the specific tract.

sections.heading: Sitting near a county line complicates title work slightly
paragraphs: Because McKenzie sits right at the edge of Conecuh County, near the Butler County line, it is worth double-checking exactly which county's records govern your specific tract before assuming where to look for deeds or probate files. We confirm this as a first step, since pulling records from the wrong courthouse wastes time.
Once we know the correct county, the research proceeds the same way it would anywhere else in south Alabama.

sections.heading: What we ask for and why
paragraphs: A deed or lease with the legal description, any recent royalty statement, and information about how you came to own the interest, whether through inheritance, purchase, or an original family reservation. Each piece helps us build an accurate picture faster and avoid asking you the same questions twice.
If you are missing some of these, that is fine, we can fill gaps using public records in most cases.

faqs.question: How do I know if my McKenzie property is actually in Conecuh County?
faqs.answer: The legal description on your deed will specify the county, and since McKenzie sits near the Butler County line, we always confirm this before pulling records.

faqs.question: Has there been oil and gas activity in this specific area?
faqs.answer: Conecuh County has seen periodic leasing tied to the regional Smackover trend, though activity directly around McKenzie has varied by specific tract and time period.

faqs.question: What if I inherited this interest but never registered with an operator?
faqs.answer: You will likely need to provide proof of inheritance, such as probate documents or an heirship affidavit, before receiving payments or completing a sale.

faqs.question: Can you help if I only know the interest exists but have no paperwork?
faqs.answer: Yes, we can search public deed and probate records to help establish and confirm ownership even starting from very little information.

faqs.question: How is a McKenzie interest valued differently from one closer to Escambia County?
faqs.answer: Without a dense, well-documented producing area nearby, McKenzie interests are generally valued more conservatively unless your specific tract has its own real production history.
